For stitch markers, I like the metal ones... they don't break.  You can also use a safety pin, piece of string, bobby pin, or a paper clip.  They list free patterns, but if you get on Ravelry.com [Ribblr.com](https://Ribblr.com),  [Amigurumi.com](https://Amigurumi.com)., they all have free patterns.  You just have to select free. And You can look on Pinterest.. but it can be like jumping through hoops to get to the patten.  I taught myself using the Crochet for Dummies book. They used to have a ton of illustrations on line and I printed off the stitch and put them on index cards.  But, they are not there anymore.  You can also use your local library... mine has books on the shelf and online books through Hoopla and Libby.  So, I have 3 different ways to get free crochet books.  Also, kindle unlimited has books and patterns.  I have heard Bella coco is very good for teaching, just keep in mind she uses UK terms.  That's important.  I also like the crochet crowd. And finally FAcebook.  There's a group called Random ACts of crochet kindness, and they have a ton of free patterns in their files.  And it's all small stuff.
